title: Bug: run logs and run view fail on Forgejo 17: bare-array job list and run numbers in URLs
body:
### describe your environment
- gt version used (`gt -v`): `gt version 1.1.0` (built with go1.27.3; openSUSE package `gitea-cli-1.1.0-1.1`)
    - [x] I also reproduced the issue [with the latest main build](https://dl.gitea.com/gitea-cli/main/)

      v1.1.0 is the same commit as `main` today (44915d2). I first filed this with 0.1.0 and the results were the same.
- Gitea version used: none; the server is **Forgejo 17.0.1** (codefloe.com). `/api/v1/version` returns `17.0.1`, and `/api/forgejo/v1/version` returns `17.0.1+gitea-1.22.0`.
    - [ ] the issue only occurred after updating gitea recently
- operating system: openSUSE Tumbleweed
- I make use of...
    - [ ] non-standard default branch names (no `main`,`master`, or `trunk`)
    - [ ] .ssh/config or .gitconfig host aliases in my git remotes
    - [ ] ssh_agent or similar
    - [ ] non-standard ports for gitea and/or ssh
    - [x] something else that's likely to interact badly with gt: the server is Forgejo, not Gitea

Please provide the output of `git remote -v` (if the issue is related to gt not finding resources on Gitea):
```
codefloe	https://codefloe.com/mcepl/rope-language-server.git (fetch)
codefloe	ssh://git@codefloe.com/mcepl/rope-language-server.git (push)
```

### describe the issue (observed vs expected behaviour)

I know Forgejo support is best effort, as #56 says, and this is not a request for full compatibility. #56 fixed the missing `actions/workflows` endpoint (#53, #54), and `gt run list` now works here with a warning. On Forgejo 17 two more differences stop `gt run view`, `gt run jobs` and `gt run logs`. Both look small, so I'm reporting them in case they're worth the same kind of fallback. If Forgejo is out of scope for these commands, please close this.

In the examples, `R` is `--host codefloe.com -R mcepl/rope-language-server`.

**1. The job listing is a bare JSON array.**

Forgejo 17 has `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run}/jobs`, which Forgejo 15 lacked (#53), but it returns a list instead of Gitea's `{"total_count": …, "jobs": […]}`:

```
$ gt api --host codefloe.com repos/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/runs/67975/jobs
[{"id":146058,"run_id":67975,"attempt":1,…,"name":"Linux Py3.11","html_url":"https://codefloe.com/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/runs/48/jobs/0/attempt/1",…,"task_id":140389,"status":"success"}, …]
```

Every command that lists the jobs of a run stops there, even when the job is given:

```
$ gt run view $R 67975
Error: Gitea returned an invalid JSON response
$ gt run jobs $R 67975
Error: Gitea returned an invalid JSON response
$ gt run logs $R 67975 --job 146061
Error: Gitea returned an invalid JSON response
$ gt run view --debug $R 67975
[debug] GET https://codefloe.com/api/v1/repos/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/workflows -> 404 Not Found (122ms): 404 page not found
[debug] GET https://codefloe.com/api/v1/repos/mcepl/rope-language-server -> 200 OK (69ms)
[debug] GET https://codefloe.com/api/v1/repos/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/runs/67975 -> 200 OK (79ms)
[debug] GET https://codefloe.com/api/v1/repos/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/runs/67975/jobs?limit=100&page=1 -> 200 OK (47ms)
Error: Gitea returned an invalid JSON response
```

`Actions.JobsPage` decodes into `ActionsWorkflowJobsResponse` and turns only a 404 into a `CapabilityError`. The logs themselves are reachable: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/146061/logs` returns the plain-text log on Forgejo 17. Accepting a bare array as well as the object, or treating an undecodable listing like a missing one, would probably be enough for `run view`, `run jobs` and `run logs`.

**2. Forgejo's web URLs hold run numbers, not run IDs.**

The comment in `parseRefURL` says that since Gitea 1.26 the web URL holds the run ID and the job ID. Forgejo still uses the run's number in the repository and the job's position in the run. Run 67975 above is `/actions/runs/48`, and its fourth job (ID 146061) is `/actions/runs/48/jobs/3/attempt/1`. `gt pr checks` prints these URLs, because they're the commit statuses' target URLs, and `gt run list` shows the ID next to a URL with the number:

```
$ gt pr checks $R 20
Linux tests / Linux Py3.11 (pull_request)	success	Successful in 1m51s	https://codefloe.com/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/runs/48/jobs/0
…
$ gt run list $R -L 1
! workflow listing is unsupported: the server does not provide GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows
success		67975				pull_request			https://codefloe.com/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/runs/48
$ gt run logs $R https://codefloe.com/mcepl/rope-language-server/actions/runs/48/jobs/3
Error: run 48 not found in mcepl/rope-language-server
```

Forgejo's run objects include the number as `index_in_repo` (`{"id": 67975, "index_in_repo": 48, "html_url": ".../actions/runs/48"}`), so a fallback could map the number to an ID when the ID lookup returns 404. The job part would be the position in the job list, not an ID.

**A side note on detecting Forgejo**, in case it helps: `comparableVersion` expects Forgejo to report a version such as `11.0.0+gitea-1.22.0`. Forgejo 17 returns plain `17.0.1` from `/api/v1/version`, so gt takes it for a Gitea version:

```
$ gt project workflow list 1 $R
Error: gt project workflow list requires Gitea 29 or newer; https://codefloe.com runs Gitea 17.0.1
```

The refusal is right, since Forgejo 17 is based on Gitea 1.22, but the message is not. Only `/api/forgejo/v1/version` carries the `+gitea-1.22.0` suffix.

Expected: `gt run logs <URL from gt pr checks>` shows the job's log on Forgejo, or at least fails with a message that says the server is not supported, as #56 does for missing endpoints.
